doc.title: Evan Christopher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 1, 2009

title: Wishing the music business were worse; touring 150 days and no manager
summary: Christopher explains his joke about the music business, turning 40, and the strain of travel. He is on the road about 150 days a year and has no management.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Okay. I’ll bet you can. When the students were asking you about making a living and how’s the music business, and I think I asked you the same thing, you sounded like you were semi-joking, but that you said I wish the music business was a little worse, because then I would do something else.

Yeah. Things are bad, but if they would just get a little bit worse then I would be forced to do something else. Yeah. Meaning that of course at the end of the day I mean there’s a lot of great things about being a musician, but then, you know, there’s aspects of it that are daunting and — I just turned 40 — and there is something about that number that makes it a little — something about that number that started making it a little harder to determine whether or not I had enough fortitude or energy to continue to deal with the adversity aspects of it, like travel for instance.
You said you’re on the road more than 100 days a year.

Probably closer to 150. And I only calculate that but they say I’m gone three months for the summer, that’s 90, and if I’m gone a week during the other months of the year, that’s 63 days left over, so that’s about 150 days. So it’s got to be somewhere around there. It certainly can’t be any less.
I’m going to ask you to move your mic out a little bit. I just don’t want to have an issue with that later. And the adversity of being — are you your own manager so to speak?

I don’t have management right now. Yeah. So it’s something that I’m considering changing very soon. It hasn’t been an issue because I haven’t been doing much of my own music until more recently, and I haven’t been doing projects that are so different that © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
they demand different types of marketing or negotiating skills, but that’s starting to come and that’s something that’s not an area that I want to be expending energy in also.
